[2026-10-27] rc:4391033521 inline on depends/hosts/darwin.mk by hebasto (member):
[quoted text omitted]

The linker stamps the SDK version into the binary. At runtime, Apple’s frameworks read it to decide which generation of behaviour the binary opts into, independently of the headers actually used and of the minimum supported macOS version.

Choosing 26.1 means the binary opts into every behaviour change Apple has gated up to macOS 26.1, so on any OS that has them, the latest ones are used.

Choosing 15.0 means the binary opts into changes gated up to macOS 15.0 and keeps the legacy behaviour for anything gated later.

This choice affects the look-and-feel of the GUI. Consider the following side-by-side comparison of `OSX_SDK_VERSION=14.0` and `OSX_SDK_VERSION=26.1` on macOS 27.2:

Though, I still wonder why this is not 26.1 now (i.e. the latest SDK), so that any OS can use the latest features, if it has them. Is there some requirement that GUI looks the same for any macOS version? Or is this some hack in the assumption that gating the features will avoid having an exploding test matrix?

Personally, I think it is fine to  let the GUI look different (possibly "modern" on later macOS versions). Also I think it is fine to use other SDK features on later macOS versions. If there was a bug in any of them, we'd have to fix them anyway for self-compilation and if there is a macOS bug a feature gate is no guarantee that the bug won't happen?

Just curious. Any value here seems fine, given your reply.
